q: Which has a lower carbon footprint, a clay idol or a plaster of Paris idol?
title: Clay idol vs plaster of Paris idol
short: An unfired clay idol usually has the lower footprint: the clay needs little processing. Plaster of Paris is made by heating gypsum, which burns fuel. Paints, transport and the frame add to both. For a fair figure, weigh the materials and include the fuel behind the plaster.
audience: Idol makers, puja committees and event organisers

ul: Plaster of Paris: fuel to calcine gypsum.
Clay idols: digging, transport and drying, usually small.
Both: paints, decorations, scaffolding and transport.

p: Water pollution from immersion is a separate issue from greenhouse gases; this page covers carbon only.

senseible: Senseible reads bills, fuel invoices and production records into dated, fingerprinted records, so the figure you send a buyer can be traced to its documents.
